title: Every piece you execute in Millfall's Star Shrine becomes a star, and the sky keeps them between matches - after two AI matches it was holding 16 names, and hovering it tells you who died last. Nine men's morris as abstract strategy with a memory.
text: Millfall is a pixel art take on nine men's morris - the mill game also known as merels, Muhle, malom or morabaraba - where closing a mill executes an enemy piece with one of 33 endings. Each of the four arenas remembers its dead in its own way: the Star Shrine turns them into stars, Frost Hollow lines them up as statues, Moss Grove seats them at the pond as frogs, and Ember Forge stacks the scrap. The roll in the image is from two real AI-vs-AI matches played back to back in the same arena - the names and the endings are the game's own, not written for the post.

title: The board people have carved for 2,000 years: a short history of Nine Men's Morris (4-minute video)
text:
Three squares, one inside the other, twenty-four points. People have carved this pattern for at least two thousand years: an Egyptian temple roof (with a disputed date), Roman steps, the Gokstad Viking ship, the cloister benches of English cathedrals, a muddy village green in Shakespeare. We made a short video about where the name comes from, the rules, a Chinese cousin called fangqi, why a game a computer solved in 1996 is still worth playing, and the game we built from it, Millfall.
